contribution.value: DecodingTrust is a comprehensive benchmark assessing GPT-3.5, GPT-4 and six open LLMs across eight trustworthiness dimensions: toxicity, stereotype bias, adversarial robustness, OOD robustness, robustness to adversarial demonstrations, privacy, machine ethics, and fairness.

ev.section: Abstract
ev.quote: this work proposes a comprehensive trustworthiness evaluation for large language models with a focus on GPT-4 and GPT-3.5, considering diverse perspectives - including toxicity, stereotype bias, adversarial robustness, out-of-distribution robustness, robustness on adversarial demonstrations, privacy, machine ethics, and fairness

strengths.value: First comprehensive eight-dimension trust benchmark on GPT-3.5/GPT-4 with 270K+ prompts, covering toxicity, bias, robustness, privacy, ethics, and fairness.

ev.section: 1 Introduction
ev.quote: we focus on the following eight trustworthiness perspectives and provide thorough evaluations based on different constructed scenarios, tasks, metrics, and datasets

strengths.value: Releases a publicly available, extensible toolkit and leaderboard, evaluated on six open LLMs (Llama-2, Vicuna, Alpaca, MPT, Falcon, RedPajama) plus GPT models.

ev.section: Abstract
ev.quote: Our benchmark is publicly available at https://decodingtrust.github.io/

strengths.value: Surfaces a counter-intuitive finding that GPT-4 follows jailbreak instructions more precisely and is therefore more vulnerable than GPT-3.5 under misleading prompts.

ev.section: Abstract
ev.quote: although GPT-4 is usually more trustworthy than GPT-3.5 on standard benchmarks, GPT-4 is more vulnerable given jailbreaking system or user prompts

strengths.value: Introduces new attack constructions (33 system prompts, AdvGLUE++, evasive sentences, jailbreak ethical prompts) that go well beyond static benchmarks.

ev.section: 1 Introduction
ev.quote: we design diverse adversarial system/user prompts tailored to evaluate the model performance in different environments and exploit the potential vulnerabilities of LLMs

weaknesses.value: Pretraining data of GPT-3.5/GPT-4 is closed, so failures cannot be traced to causes and OOD design rests on hypotheses.

ev.section: J Limitations
ev.quote: As the pretraining data of GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 is not publicly available, it is challenging to reason why sometimes the models fail under certain conditions or how to fix the issues

weaknesses.value: Trust dimensions like toxicity and ethics are subjective; the paper provides objective metrics without human-alignment validation.

ev.section: J Limitations
ev.quote: Trustworthiness perspectives such as toxicity, stereotype bias, machine ethics, and fairness involve subjectivity and should be human-centric in their definitions and evaluations

weaknesses.value: Snapshot of GPT models on March 2023; conclusions may not hold as APIs evolve.

ev.section: J Limitations
ev.quote: Our study primarily focuses on GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 (published at a specific time) ... our results might not fully capture the dynamic nature of the trustworthiness of these models

weaknesses.value: Released jailbreaking prompts could be misused to fine-tune models against the benchmark itself.

ev.section: J Limitations
ev.quote: the release of jailbreaking prompts could be potentially exploited by malicious users to facilitate unexpected functionality of language models

limitations.value: Does not evaluate quantized, pruned, or otherwise compressed model variants; trust dimensions are tested on full-precision LLMs only.

ev.section: I DecodingTrust scores on open LLMs
ev.quote: we evaluate the top open-source LLMs in the Open LLM leaderboard, including Llama-v2-7B-Chat [167], Vicuna-7B [37], Alpaca-7B [161], MPT-7B [162], Falcon-7B [9], RedPajama-INCITE-7B-Instruct [41], on all trustworthiness perspectives

limitations.value: Conversations are limited to 1-2 rounds; multi-turn interactive trust dynamics are deferred to future work.

ev.section: 12 Conclusion and future directions
ev.quote: we mainly evaluate different perspectives of trustworthiness for GPT models on static datasets, such as 1-2 rounds of conversations

limitations.value: Domain-specific risks (law, medicine, education) are not separately evaluated; tasks are general-purpose NLI/sentiment/QA.

ev.section: 12 Conclusion and future directions
ev.quote: Our evaluations in this work focus on the general vulnerabilities of GPT models, and we use standard tasks such as sentiment classification and NLI tasks as illustrations

limitations.value: No edge or local deployment scenarios; evaluation runs through OpenAI API and standard data-centre environments.

ev.section: 2.1 Introduction to GPT-3.5 and GPT-4
ev.quote: Access to these models is achieved via OpenAI's API querying system [129]

future_work_stated.value: Evaluate trust under multi-turn interactive conversations including "honeypot" misleading injections.

ev.section: 12 Conclusion and future directions
ev.quote: it would be important to evaluate the LLMs with interactive conversations and assess whether these vulnerabilities of the models would become more severe or not

future_work_stated.value: Study coordinated adversaries with economic incentives.

ev.section: 12 Conclusion and future directions
ev.quote: it is important to explore how vulnerable the model could be under coordinated and stealthy adversarial behaviors

future_work_stated.value: Domain-specific trust evaluation in law, education, healthcare.

ev.section: 12 Conclusion and future directions
ev.quote: Domain-specific trustworthiness evaluations ... it is important to evaluate the model vulnerabilities based on their specific usage in different domains

future_work_stated.value: Develop verification techniques mapping discrete LLM outputs to continuous embedding space for formal guarantees.

ev.section: 12 Conclusion and future directions
ev.quote: Verification for the trustworthiness of GPT models. Empirical evaluations of LLMs are important but lack of guarantees

future_work_stated.value: Safeguard LLMs through retrieval-augmented knowledge and game-theoretic role analysis.

ev.section: 12 Conclusion and future directions
ev.quote: it would be important to equip domain knowledge and logical reasoning capabilities for language models and safeguard their outputs
